seats.title: Provost

policies.label: Spend on the academic side
policies.note: Takes the thorough way, and the bill

policies.label: Keep the faculty with you
policies.note: Takes whichever way lands best in the common room

seats.blurb: Runs the academic routine: the timetable, the committees, the things that do not need a President.
seats.outsideLine: An outside appointment, from a college with a better library and worse weather. Expensive, and good.
seats.internalLine: Promoted from the roster. Cheaper, popular, and no longer teaching anything.

seats.title: Dean

policies.label: Back the school’s requests
policies.note: Takes the thorough way, and the bill

policies.label: Keep the department happy
policies.note: Takes whichever way lands best in the common room

seats.blurb: Runs one school's routine, which is mostly other people's timetables and one long-running dispute.
seats.outsideLine: An outside dean, who will mention their previous institution.
seats.internalLine: One of the school's own, promoted out of the classroom.

seats.title: Facilities Director

policies.label: Cheapest fix first
policies.note: Patches, defers, and keeps the bill down

policies.label: Worst first, properly
policies.note: Fixes what is worst, at what it costs

seats.blurb: Triages the estate: the roof, the boiler, the thing in the basement, without asking first.
seats.outsideLine: A professional, from a hospital trust. Knows what a survey is for.
seats.internalLine: The longest-serving member of the roster, who has been doing half of this anyway.

seats.title: Dean of Students

policies.label: Hold the line
policies.note: Cheap, and they know where they stand

policies.label: Fix what they are asking about

seats.blurb: Handles student life: the letters, the petitions, the occupation of the foyer, before they reach the President.
seats.outsideLine: From a larger college, with a folder of policies already written.
seats.internalLine: A member of the roster the students already go to.

seats.title: VP of Advancement

policies.label: Ask sparingly
policies.note: The ledger stays warm and gives less

policies.label: Ask properly, and often
policies.note: The ledger gives more and cools

seats.blurb: Runs the donor routine — the letters, the visits, the annual fund. Runs the campaigns, too.
seats.outsideLine: A professional fundraiser, who will want a budget and a title.
seats.internalLine: Someone from the roster who is unusually good with people, and will stop teaching.

rules.thrifty: Takes the choice that spends least.
rules.thorough: Takes the choice that spends most, which is usually the one that fixes it.
rules.popular: Takes the choice the students feel best about.

lines.payrollNote: Every seat is permanent payroll and a step of the administrative ratchet: once filled, a seat is never cheaper to empty than to keep.
lines.escalated: Too large to delegate; this one reaches the President.
lines.speedNote: Fast time is bought with administrative capacity: 4× needs a Provost, 8× a Provost and four Deans.
lines.noSchools: A Dean needs a school to be dean of.
lines.noSenior: Nobody on the roster is senior enough for this.
lines.noSchoolSenior: Nobody in this school is senior enough yet: a Dean comes from their own faculty.
